concerns.text: Task T013 mandates a specific MICE convergence threshold (mean absolute diff < 0.01) and a fallback to listwise deletion for predictors if failed. The Spec (FR-004) only requires MICE for predictors and listwise deletion for outcomes. This task introduces a silent weakening of the FR-004 requirement by adding a hard failure condition for predictor imputation that is not authorized by the spec, potentially causing the pipeline to halt or degrade data quality (via listwise deletion of predictors) contrary to the spec's intent of preserving predictor data via MICE.

Task T027b implements a 'Single Group Handling' logic (logging W-STRAT-SINGLE-001 and skipping stratification) if only one valid platform exists. Spec FR-005 mandates stratification by 'all available platforms' meeting N>=30. While the logic is sensible, the task introduces a specific behavioral deviation (skipping the step entirely) and a new error code not defined in the spec. This constitutes a silent narrowing of the FR-005 requirement, as the spec does not explicitly authorize skipping the stratification step if only one group exists, only excluding invalid groups.

Tasks T070 and T071 block the entire project on a 'future discovery' of a verified data source. The Spec (US-1) requires ingestion of the Cyberbullying Survey 2021. If T070 fails to find a verified source, the task description implies the project halts without a defined fallback path (e.g., 'halt with E-NO-SOURCE'). This creates a risk of the pipeline being unable to proceed without a clear, spec-aligned failure mode, effectively weakening the project's ability to deliver a result even if the data source is simply unverified but the data exists. The task must explicitly define the failure path (halt with specific error) to preserve the constraint of 'Real Data Only' without creating an undefined blocking state.
